title: Insurance Coverage & Claims Training Note: Share of Order Reductions on Authorization Corrections
content:
**Training note — Insurance Coverage & Claims, authorization corrections (CO-197).** Questions and answers on the authorization correction's share of the order's reductions.

**What is the share?**
The authorization correction's share of the order's reductions is the denial's amount divided by all the denied amounts on the claim where the remittance paid at least one line of the claim; it is the denial's amount divided by the amount the claim billed at filing where no line was paid but the plan adjudicated a line to the member or to a contractual adjustment; otherwise it is one.

**What does the share act on?**
Under the authorization correction, the reductions are multiplied by the share.

**What counts as "all the denied amounts on the claim"?**
Every denial line on the claim, whatever its code, the authorization denial included.

**What counts as a line adjudicated to the member or to a contractual adjustment?**
A member-responsibility line or a contractual-adjustment line on the claim.

**Worked question (hypothetical).** A claim billed 800.00 USD; its remittance paid one line of 300.00 USD, wrote off 100.00 USD and denied 250.00 USD as CO-197 and 150.00 USD as CO-50. A line was paid, so the share is 250.00 divided by 400.00 (all the denied amounts), that is 0.625.

**Worked question (hypothetical).** A claim billed 500.00 USD; its remittance paid nothing, assigned 40.00 USD to the member and denied 460.00 USD as CO-197. No line was paid but one was adjudicated to the member, so the share is 460.00 divided by 500.00, that is 0.92.

**And where the remittance paid nothing and adjudicated nothing to the member or to a contractual adjustment?** The share is one: the reductions are taken in full.
